chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man takes the zakat, it is like his own wealth; he does with it whatever he wishes. He said, and he said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed a duty upon the wealth of the rich for the poor, a duty for which they are not praised except by fulfilling it, and it is the zakat. So when it reaches the poor, it is at the status of his own wealth; he does with it whatever he wishes.

I said, 'Does he marry with it and perform Hajj from it?' He said, 'Yes, it is his wealth.' I said, 'So is the poor person rewarded if he performs Hajj from the zakat just as the rich person, the owner of the wealth, is rewarded?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.يَصْنَعُ بِهَا مَا يَشَاءُ: He does with it whatever he wishes

ai.seo_question: Does zakat become the full property of the poor recipient, and can they use it for Hajj or marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential status of zakat as full private property (mal) for the recipient, distinguishing it from a loan or trust that requires specific accounting. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the poor person earns the same spiritual reward for acts of worship funded by zakat as a wealthy person would, emphasizing that the merit lies in the act of worship itself rather than the source of funds. This ruling underscores the generosity of the divine command, ensuring that the poor are not restricted in how they utilize the wealth designated for their purification and sustenance.
